summary: Openfire is a real-time collaboration server that facilitates instant messaging and chat infrastructure. Built on Java and distributed under the Apache-2.0 licence, it handles client connections for XMPP-based communication networks. It provides a centralised backend for managing users, routing messages, and administering chat services across an organisation.
goodFor: It is a solid fit if you need to run an internal, self-hosted XMPP messaging network behind your own firewall.
watchOut: Managing a Java-based enterprise server can introduce significant operational overhead regarding memory tuning, security updates, and configuration management compared to lighter alternatives.
deployNotes: Because it runs on Java, you will typically need to provision a compatible runtime environment, configure persistent storage for chat logs and user data, and set up a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
